claims.claim: Southern Copper sits on a durable electrification/infrastructure bottleneck because copper is a required conductive material across grids, motors, industrial equipment and data-center power systems; its operating leverage is therefore to copper availability and price rather than to one downstream technology.

Tía María provides a concrete supply-expansion bridge, but the causal path from scarcity to shareholder value is conditional on permitting/social acceptance, construction execution, grades and realized copper prices.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Owned copper reserves/production capacity participate directly in a difficult-to-substitute physical bottleneck.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Copper demand spans multiple infrastructure and electrification scenarios, while commodity-price and project-execution sensitivity remain material.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Aluminum and efficiency gains can substitute in some applications, but broad copper conductivity/use requirements preserve substantial demand resilience.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Mine ownership gives upstream control, but jurisdiction, grades, water, permitting and project timing are concentrated physical constraints.

causalEdges.relation: increases realized-price operating leverage, conditional on volume/cost
adds future production capacity if schedule and social/permitting conditions hold
reduces copper demand in technically/economically substitutable uses

risks.risk: Successor bottlenecks can shift from copper availability to permitting, water, grid interconnection, construction capacity or customer affordability; copper scarcity alone does not guarantee project value capture.

contradictions.claim: Record financial acceleration coexisted with lower copper sales volume.
contradictions.resolution: This strengthens the commodity-price leverage thesis but weakens any claim that current earnings growth proves operating-volume expansion.

unknowns.unknown: Long-run application-level substitution elasticity between copper, aluminum and design efficiency is not established by the current company evidence.

claims.claim: The strongest present falsification pressure is that Q2 earnings growth was price-led while copper sales volume fell, so extrapolating record earnings as proof of operating expansion would inflate confidence.

The $1.25B debt financing improves project funding visibility but increases fixed financing exposure before Tía María contributes production, making schedule slippage more consequential rather than inherently disqualifying.

factors.name: commodity-price dependence
factors.basis: Current earnings acceleration depended materially on higher realized metal prices.

factors.name: financing/dilution
factors.basis: Debt rather than equity avoids immediate dilution but adds fixed obligations ahead of project cash generation.

factors.name: concentration/governance
factors.basis: Large mining projects remain exposed to jurisdictional, social-license and execution concentration; current Beta evidence does not establish a governance defect.

factors.name: backlog/TAM discipline
factors.basis: No backlog/TAM claim is needed for the thesis; project completion and realized production are the relevant falsifiable measures.

causalEdges.relation: can reverse price-led operating leverage even if strategic copper demand remains intact

risks.risk: Commodity-price reversal can overwhelm modest operating progress.
Project delays or cost escalation can raise carrying costs and defer the supply-growth thesis.
Substitution and recycling can moderate scarcity economics at the margin even when absolute copper demand remains durable.

contradictions.claim: Record earnings imply broad operating momentum.
contradictions.resolution: Partially falsified: the evidence supports strong financial momentum but not broad volume momentum because copper sales volume declined 1.5% year over year.

unknowns.unknown: Beta has not independently quantified valuation/crowding or future copper prices; these remain non-gating and belong outside this perspective's canonical authority.
